macros.name: clip
macros.doc: You can use the \clip command to clip all subsequent drawing.

macros.name: fill
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path[fill].

macros.name: filldraw
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path[fill,draw].

macros.name: matrix
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path node[matrix].

macros.name: nodepart
macros.doc: It will stop the typesetting of whatever node part was typeset until now and then start putting all following text into the node part named ⟨part name⟩ – until another \nodepart is encountered or until the node ⟨text⟩ ends.

macros.name: pattern
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path[pattern].

macros.name: pic
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path pic.

macros.name: scoped
macros.doc: This command works like \tikz, only you can use it inside a {tikzpicture}.

macros.name: shade
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path[shade].

macros.name: shadedraw
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path[shade,draw].

macros.name: tikz
macros.doc: This command places the ⟨path commands⟩ inside a {tikzpicture} environment.

macros.name: tikzdeclarecoordinatesystem
macros.doc: This command declares a new coordinate system named ⟨name⟩ that can later on be used by writing (⟨name⟩ cs:⟨arguments⟩).

macros.name: tikzlastnode
macros.doc: Expands to the last node on the path.

macros.name: tikzset
macros.doc: This command will process the ⟨options⟩ using the \pgfkeys command, documented in detail in Section 87, with the default path set to /tikz.

macros.name: useasboundingbox
macros.doc: Inside {tikzpicture} this is an abbreviation for \path[use as bounding box].

envs.name: scope
envs.doc: This environment takes graphic options as an optional argument and these options apply to everything inside the scope, but not to anything outside.

envs.name: tikzpicture
envs.doc: In LaTeX this is done using the environment {tikzpicture}, in plain TeX you just use \tikzpicture to start the picture and \endtikzpicture to end it.
